title: Continuous NDJSON embedding ingest with idempotent retries and async job API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: customers ingest large corpora for embedding indexing (millions of documents). The existing synchronous single-request embedding API leads to timeouts, high retry pressure, and inconsistent cost accounting. Goal: provide a robust streaming/bulk ingestion surface that supports newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) and gRPC streaming, server-side chunking, explicit async job semantics, and idempotent retries so clients can reliably upload large datasets with predictable latency and cost.

Scope: implement a new /v1/embeddings/bulk-stream endpoint that accepts NDJSON over HTTP chunked transfer, plus a matching gRPC streaming endpoint. Implement async job lifecycle (enqueue -> processing -> complete/failed) surfaced via job IDs and webhooks. Core features:
- Idempotency keys per logical batch with de-duplication window and idempotency metadata persisted for 7 days.
- Exactly-once output at the logical-document level via dedupe layer + idempotency receipts (best-effort for on-prem Dedicated environments).
- Backpressure signals: HTTP 429 with Retry-After when server buffer is saturated; gRPC flow-control for streaming clients.
- At-least-once worker processing internally for durability; dedupe at storage layer to avoid duplicate embeddings.
- Bulk acknowledgement model: incremental ACKs (every N documents) to allow tail latency visibility.
- Retry strategy: client-side exponential backoff with capped jitter; server-side idempotency allows safe retries.
- Monitoring: per-job metrics (throughput, errors, avg embedding latency, token consumption), per-tenant quotas and cost breakdown exported to Console.

Non-goals: building a full ETL pipeline or long-term data retention policy (beyond short idempotency metadata). This ticket focuses on transport, job semantics, retry/dedupe, and a storage-friendly ingest path.

design_decisions: 1) Transport formats: primary NDJSON over HTTP chunked for ease-of-use; optional gRPC streaming for high-throughput clients. 2) Idempotency: server stores idempotency_key -> job_id mapping and per-document dedupe tokens for 7 days. 3) Exactly-once at logical-document level implemented by dedupe bloom-filter + compact dedupe table (best-effort), combined with idempotency_key to present deterministic jobs to callers. 4) Backpressure: server will return 429/Retry-After and emit 'backpressure' metric; gRPC will use flow-control window adjustments. 5) Storage: write-optimized embedding table partitioned by tenant and job_date to speed bulk writes and deletes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for NDJSON parser and idempotency store.
- Integration test simulating retries and duplicate batches (verify no duplicates persisted).
- Load test: sustained 5 GB/min ingest with mixed doc sizes, measure p95 ingest latency and token cost.
- Canary: Gradual rollout to 5% inbound bulk jobs over 72 hours; monitor job success rate and memory usage.
- Chaos test: inject worker restart during processing and confirm idempotency prevents duplication.
rollout_checklist:
- Implement feature flag 'embeds.bulk_stream' behind runtime config.
- Unit + integration test coverage >= 85%.
- SRE runbook for OOM/backpressure events.
- Console UI: job listing, per-job cost estimate, ability to abort job.
- Webhook delivery retrier (exponential backoff) for job-complete notifications.
- Add telemetry: per-tenant bytes_in, docs_processed, duplicate_count, avg_embedding_ms.
- Security sign-off for idempotency metadata retention.
open_questions:
- Dedup window length: 7 days default vs customer-configurable? (SRE prefers shorter windows to reduce storage).
- Exact format for incremental ACKs (JSON lines vs protobuf).
- How to surface partial failures to callers: job-level 'partial_success' vs per-doc error mapping?

3) Wire job lifecycle into Console and webhook system.
4) Start canary for hosted customers and gather telemetry.
5) Document compatibility notes for Dedicated/Private (on-prem may require idempotency retention disabled).
